question_text: A set X consists of 10 integers with an average value of 6. The elements are arranged in ascending order. The smallest 5 elements are replaced by the largest 5 elements to form a new set Y. The average of set Y becomes 9. What is the average of the largest 5 elements in set X?
explanation: The sum of the 10 elements in set X is 10 * 6 = 60. Let the sum of the smallest 5 elements be S1 and the sum of the largest 5 be S2. So, S1 + S2 = 60. When the smallest 5 are replaced by the largest 5, the new set Y essentially contains two copies of the largest 5 elements. The sum of set Y is 10 * 9 = 90. This means 2 * S2 = 90, which makes S2 = 45. The average of these largest 5 elements is S2 / 5 = 45 / 5 = 9.
